The largest country in the world is Russia.

To understand the concept of relativity, imagine time as a river flowing at a steady pace for everyone. In our everyday lives, we assume this river flows at the same speed for everyone, everywhere. However, Einstein’s theory of relativity suggests that this "river" can actually speed up or slow down depending on how fast you are moving or how strong the gravity is around you.

Think of it like a rubber band. If you stretch the rubber band (by moving very fast, close to the speed of light), it becomes longer and thinner. In this analogy, the "stretching" represents time slowing down. So, if you were on a super-fast train moving near the speed of light, your personal experience of time would feel completely normal, just like the rubber band feels normal to you while you hold it. But to someone standing still on the platform watching you zoom by, your time would appear to be moving much slower than theirs, just as the stretched rubber band looks longer and different from their perspective.

Similarly, gravity acts like a heavy weight placed on the rubber band. The stronger the gravity (like being near a massive planet or black hole), the more "stretched" or distorted time becomes, causing it to tick slower compared to areas with weaker gravity. This is why time passes slightly differently for satellites in orbit than it does for us on the ground, a fact that GPS systems must account for to give you accurate directions.
